mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a rise in unemployment (UNRATE) above 6% signals weakening aggregate demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly negative at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase of more than 0.3 percentage points in the unemployment rate for three consecutive months signals labor market weakening, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises by >0.3pp for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative in at least 60% of triggered periods at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% over four consecutive months signals contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >1% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not significantly different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both the housing starts index (HOUST) and personal savings rate (RSAFS) above their 12-month moving averages signals a shift from saving to investment, which boosts future earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month MA AND RSAFS > 12-month MA in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive in at least 60% of triggered episodes at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate held below 1% for more than six consecutive months in a low-inflation environment signals accommodative monetary policy, which supports risk asset valuations and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive in at least 50% of triggered episodes at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly payroll employment increase (PAYEMS) of less than 50,000 for three consecutive months signals persistent labor market slack, which depresses wage growth and corporate profitability, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change < 50,000 for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative in at least 60% of triggered episodes at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year increase of more than 4% in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) alongside a stable unemployment rate (UNRATE < 6%) signals robust aggregate demand, which supports earnings growth and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive in at least 60% of triggered episodes at 5% significance.
